title: encrypt: P-384 KARI wraps 16-byte AES-128 CEK with AES-192-KW producing mismatched KEK
description: In encrypt.rs the CEK is always a 16-byte AES-128-CBC key. For P-384 recipients, build_p384_recipient() uses DH_SHA384_KDF + AES-192-KW. AES-192-KW correctly wraps a 16-byte key (AES-KW accepts any multiple of 8 bytes ≥ 16). The resulting wrapped key is 24 bytes. A compliant decryptor using AES-192-KW will unwrap to 16 bytes and use it for AES-128-CBC decryption — this works. The bug is a security level mismatch: P-384 provides ~192-bit security but content is only protected by 128-bit AES. RFC 5753 does not forbid this combination but it is an unusual pairing. A more conformant implementation would use AES-256-CBC + AES-256-KW for P-384 recipients. This is a security property deficiency, not a protocol correctness failure — decryption roundtrips correctly.
